prompt: Write an essay about distance learning and whether online classes can replace classroom learning.
text:
Distance learning is a very important topic in our days. Nowadays, many students are studying from home with the computer. In my opinion, distance learning have advantages and disadvantages, but I think it cannot replace the classroom learning completely.

First, the main advantage is the flexibility. Students can to study in any place and at any time, so it is very convenient for people who work or who have family responsibilities. For example, my cousin works in a restaurant in the evenings, and distance learning permits him to study in the morning. Also, is cheaper because you do not need to pay for transport.

However, there are big problems. The teacher cannot see if the student is understanding or not. Also, the students feel lonely and they lose motivation. In my experience during the pandemic, I was very distracted at home because my brothers were always making noise. It was difficult for me to concentrate, and my grades were more lower than before.

Another problem is the technology. Not all families have good internet or a laptop. This makes the education unfair, because rich students have more opportunities than poor students.

In conclusion, I believe that distance learning is useful but the classroom is more better for the learning and social development. The best solution is maybe a combination of both systems, because we can take the advantages of each one. Finally, the most important thing is that the education must be accessible for everyone.

prompt: Write an essay about distance learning and whether online classes can replace classroom learning.
text:
Distance learning has become very popular in recent years. In my opinion, distance learning is useful but it cannot replace the traditional classroom completely. Many students think online class is convenient, but they also face some problems.

Firstly, distance learning gives students more freedom. For example, last semester I took an online course about computer programming. I could watch the lecture at night after I finished my part-time job. If I had to go to the campus, I would not have time for it. So for busy people, the online course is a good choice.

However, there are also disadvantages. When I studied online, I felt very lonely because I did not meet my classmates. The teacher also could not see my face clearly, so she did not know when I was confused. Yesterday I have a problem with my assignment, but I did not ask anyone because I was too shy to send a message. I waited for three days and finally I gave up the question.

In addition, the internet is not always stable. Last month the connection was broken during the exam and I lose many minutes. This was very stressful for me. Some students in my hometown do not even have a good computer, so distance learning is not fair for them.

To sum up, I think the best way is to combine online and offline learning. Students can use the internet for the lectures and go to school for discussion and practice. In this way, the education will be more effective and the students will feel more connected to the teachers.

prompt: Write an essay about distance learning and whether online classes can replace classroom learning.
text:
Distance learning has changed how a lot of students study. Online courses offer real advantages in flexibility and access, but they also raise questions about engagement, fairness, and quality. I think distance learning can help traditional classrooms, but it cant fully replace them. School gives you structure and people around you, and online learning often just doesnt provide that.

The biggest benefit is flexibility. Students who work part-time, take care of family, or live far from campus can watch lectures when it works for them. Recorded sessions also let you pause and rewind the hard parts, which you cant really do in a packed lecture hall. For a lot of adults going back to school, that flexibility is the difference between enrolling and giving up.

But being apart makes things harder. Teachers have a tough time noticing when someone is confused or checked out. Students feel isolated without the random conversations before and after class. Its easy to lose motivation when nobody is checking in on you in person. A lot of people dont realize how much they depend on routine and accountability until its gone.

Fairness is another problem. Not every household has good internet or a decent laptop. If exams depend on a stable connection, students with fewer resources get hit harder, and it isnt their fault. Schools that go online need to invest in devices, connectivity, and tech support, or the gap between students just gets bigger.

The best setup might be a mix. Lectures and practice can happen online, while discussions, labs, and mentoring stay in person. That keeps the flexibility and still protects the human side of learning. Distance learning is useful, just not as a full replacement for school.

prompt: Write an essay about distance learning and whether online classes can replace classroom learning.
text:
I'll be honest, I took my first online class in 2020 and I hated almost every minute of it. My kitchen table was my classroom, my cat kept walking across the keyboard during quizzes, and my roommate's Netflix kept buffering. So when people ask me whether distance learning works, my gut answer is no. But that's not really fair, because I also know people who thrived. My sister finished two degrees online while working nights at a hospital.

The thing is, distance learning shifts the burden onto the student. Nobody reminds you that the reading is due. Nobody notices when you slide into the back row of your own life. You have to be your own teacher and your own alarm clock, and most of us are not great at that yet. I wasn't.

Still, there's something to be said for being able to rewind a lecture at 2am. I used to miss things in big lecture halls because someone was coughing or the projector was blurry. Online I could replay the hard parts until they made sense.

Anyway, I don't think the answer is picking one side. Maybe the honest answer is that it depends on who you are and what your life looks like that month.

Speaking of the cat, she's asleep on my notes right now. Anyway.

prompt: Write an essay about what success and failure teach us.
text:
Success and failure are two words that everybody knows, but few people understand them completely. In my opinion, success is not only to get the things we want, but also to learn from our mistakes. Failure, on the other hand, is not something bad always; it can be a very good teacher.

When I was a child in Colombia, my father had a small shop. He wanted to expand the business and he borrowed money from the bank. Unfortunately, the new store did not have many customers, and after one year he had to close it. My father was very sad and he did not speak for several days. But after some time, he started to sell food in the street with my mother. Today they have a restaurant that is very successful. For me, this experience shows that failure can be the beginning of something better.

On the other side, success can also be dangerous if we do not have humility. Some people who win a lot of money or who become famous, they forget their friends and family. They think that they are better than others. This is why I think success must be balanced with good values.

In school, I also learned this lesson. When I failed my first English exam in the United States, I felt very embarrassed. However, I decided to study harder and to ask the teacher for help. In the next exam I got a B, and I was more happy than if I had passed the first time without effort.

So, in conclusion, success and failure are both necessary in life. We must not be afraid of failure because it helps us to grow. And we should remember that success is not the final destination, but a process that we are always building.

prompt: Write an essay about what success and failure teach us.
text:
Success and failure are important parts of life. Many people think success means become rich or famous, but I think success is different for each person. Failure is also not always bad, because it can teach us a lot of things.

Last year I failed my driving test for the first time. I was very nervous and I made a mistake when I was parking the car. Everybody in my family laughed at me a little, and I felt very disappointed. I wanted to give up and never drive again. However, my uncle told me that many famous people also failed many times before they succeed. He told me the story of Thomas Edison, who tried thousands of times before he made the light bulb. After that, I began to practice every weekend with my uncle. I was more careful with the mirror and the lane. Two months later I passed the test on my second try.

From this experience, I learned that failure is not the end. If we only succeed all the time, we will never know how to deal with difficulties. When I failed, I had to think about my weakness and change my method. This is a very valuable skill.

On the other hand, I think some people are too afraid of failure. They do not try new things because they worry about making mistakes. For example, my classmate wants to study abroad but she did not apply yet because she is afraid of being rejected. I think she should try, because even if she fails, she will still have experience.

In my opinion, success is the result of hard work and persistence. Failure is the teacher who shows us where we need to improve. If we can accept both of them, we will become stronger and happier in our life.

prompt: Write an essay about what success and failure teach us.
text:
We usually define success as reaching a goal and failure as falling short of one. But these definitions hide something. Success shows what we did right, while failure shows what we didnt understand yet, and that info is often more useful. Someone who never fails might never learn how to recover, adjust, or question their own assumptions.

Think about a typical school example. A student gets a bad grade on a test and has a choice. She can blame the teacher, the test, or her own lack of talent, or she can look at the specific mistakes and build a better study plan. The first option protects her ego but changes nothing. The second is uncomfortable, but it turns a setback into a lesson. Over time, students who analyze failure usually improve in ways the ones who avoid it dont.

Failure isnt automatically valuable though. Some failures come from things nobody controls, like illness, money problems, or no support at home. Telling someone struggling in those situations that their failure is a growth opportunity can put unfair blame on them. A healthy view of failure accepts personal responsibility and also recognizes luck and structure.

Success has its own risks. Achievement can make people arrogant, narrow their attention, or make them scared to take the next risk in case they lose what they got. People who define themselves only by their wins often struggle when those wins stop.

Maybe success and failure are two sides of the same process. Each one gives information and asks you to respond honestly. Living well means accepting both without letting either one define who you are.

prompt: Write an essay about what success and failure teach us.
text:
So I got rejected from the summer program I wanted most. Like, the one I'd been talking about since sophomore year. I opened the email on my phone in the grocery store parking lot, which is probably not how I imagined finding out.

Here's the thing though. I spent that whole night feeling like the failure everyone was going to think I was. Then I went back and read the feedback, which was honestly kind of helpful, and I realized my essay was weak. I'd written it in one night. Of course it didn't work.

I think success gets described as this straight line, but mine has looked more like a zigzag. I got into a state competition in eighth grade and then didn't make varsity in ninth. I got a scholarship and then lost my job the next semester. Each thing felt like the end of something.

Success is the stuff you can point to. Failure is the stuff that makes you rewrite the essay. I don't know which one matters more. Probably the rewriting.

My grandma used to say you only really know a thing once you've messed it up. She was a seamstress. She ruined a lot of wedding dresses before she was good, and she used to laugh about it.

Anyway I'm reapplying next year. The deadline is in March and I already have a draft. Wish me luck.

prompt: Write an essay about the importance of having a positive attitude.
text:
In my opinion, having a positive attitude is one of the most important things for a person's life. A positive attitude does not mean that we ignore the problems, but it means that we face them with hope and confidence. I believe that our attitude can change many situations, even when the circumstances are not good.

When I arrived in this country two years ago, I did not speak English at all. Every day was very difficult. At the beginning, I was thinking that I would never learn the language and that I should return to my country. I felt sad and I was always comparing myself with other students. However, one teacher told me that every mistake is a step to improve. She was very kind and she always smiled when I spoke. Her attitude helped me to change my mind. Now I am taking college classes and I am more confident than before.

Positive attitude is also important in the work. My mother cleans offices in the night. Sometimes her boss is very rude and the work is very tiring. But she always says that she is grateful to have a job and a family. Because of her attitude, her co-workers respect her and she received a promotion last year. I think that a positive person is more attractive to other people, and they want to help him or her.

On the other hand, I think that we must be realistic. Being positive does not mean to believe that everything will be perfect without effort. We need to work hard and to plan our goals. The attitude is the motor, but the action is the car.

In conclusion, a positive attitude can change our experiences and our relationships. It is a choice that we can make every day. If we decide to see the good side, we will find more opportunities and more happiness in our life.

prompt: Write an essay about the importance of having a positive attitude.
text:
Positive attitude is very important for people in their life. I think a person with positive attitude can solve problems better and also can make other people feel happy. Although life is not always easy, we can choose how to think about the things that happen to us.

Last year, I had a very bad time in my university. I failed two courses in the first semester and my parents were disappointed. At that time I thought I was a useless student and I did not want to go to the class. I stayed in my room all day and I played computer games. My roommate noticed that I was not happy, so he invited me to join the basketball team. At first I refused, but finally I went to the training. The coach was very encouraging. He said every player make mistakes, and the important thing is to keep trying. After several weeks, I started to feel better. I also started to study harder because I wanted to show my parents that I could change.

From this experience, I learned that attitude can change the result. When I thought negatively, I could not see any solution. When I began to believe that I could improve, I found many ways to study and to make new friends. Now I passed all my courses in the second year.

Positive attitude is not the same as ignoring problems. Some people think that being positive means to smile all the time, but this is not true. A positive person accepts that bad things happen, but he or she still looks for a way forward. For example, my grandmother lost her husband several years ago. She was very sad for a long time, but she decided to join a dance group in the park. Now she is happier and her friends say she is an inspiration.

In conclusion, I believe that positive attitude is a powerful tool. It does not solve all problems, but it helps us face them with courage and hope.

prompt: Write an essay about the importance of having a positive attitude.
text:
Positive attitude gets dismissed as a slogan, something on motivational posters more than a real factor in how people live. But research and everyday life both suggest the way we read events shapes how we respond to them. A positive attitude doesnt mean denying difficulty. It means facing difficulty while believing effort can change the outcome.

You can see the difference in a classroom. Two students struggle with the same algebra unit. One decides the struggle proves they arent good at math and stops trying. The other decides the material is hard and asks for help. Over a semester the second student usually gets further, not because shes smarter but because she keeps going when it feels bad.

It matters at work too. People tend to respond well to coworkers who stay constructive during stressful projects. They arent naive about problems, they just focus on whats next. That kind of optimism makes teams more willing to take risks and share ideas.

But positivity has limits. Forcing a smile through real grief, injustice, or illness can be unhelpful and even isolating. People need room to feel what they feel. A healthier kind of positivity admits the pain and still keeps a sense that your choices matter.

A positive attitude is less a feeling than a habit. Its built through small decisions you make over and over, and it gets easier when you see that those decisions actually help.

prompt: Write an essay about whether first impressions are accurate.
text:
First impressions are very important in our social life. When we meet someone for the first time, we usually form an opinion in a few seconds. Many people think that this opinion is always correct, but I do not agree with this idea. In my opinion, first impressions are often wrong because they are based on appearance, and we do not know the real personality of the person.

I have a personal experience about this. When I started my classes at the university in Mexico, there was a boy in my group who looked very serious. He never smiled and he was always sitting alone in the back of the room. I thought he was arrogant and I did not want to talk to him. For two months, we did not speak at all. Then one day, the professor asked us to work in pairs for a project, and we were together. I discovered that he was very funny and intelligent. He was shy, not arrogant. Now we are best friends and I am very grateful that I gave him a second chance.

However, I think that first impressions are not always negative. Sometimes they help us to be careful with people who are dangerous or dishonest. My mother says that her intuition is very strong, and she has been right many times about the people she met. The problem is when we do not change our opinion after we know more information.

Also, the first impression is very important in job interviews and in business. We need to dress well, to speak clearly, and to show confidence. But after that, the company wants to see the real skills of the person.

To conclude, I believe that first impressions are just the beginning of a relationship. We should be open to change our mind, because people are more complex than their appearance. Giving everyone a second chance is a good way to learn and to grow.

prompt: Write an essay about whether first impressions are accurate.
text:
First impression is something that people form very quickly when they meet a new person. In many cultures, first impression is considered very important. People often think that a first impression is accurate, but I am not sure about that. In my opinion, first impressions can be useful, but they can also be wrong.

When I came to the United States for my study, I had a bad first impression of my roommate. He was very loud and he always played music late at night. I thought he was rude and selfish. I decided that I would not be friend with him. For the first month, we barely talked. One night, however, I could not sleep because of my stomach pain. He saw me and he brought me medicine and hot water. He also sat with me until I felt better. At that moment I realized that I was wrong about him. He was actually a very kind and caring person. Now we are good friends, and he is like my brother.

This experience made me think about how we judge people. We usually judge them by their appearance, their accent, or their behavior in the first few minutes. But these things do not show everything about a person. Some people are shy when they meet new people, so they seem cold. Some people are nervous, so they talk too much. If we only trust our first feeling, we will miss many good friends.

Of course, first impressions are not always wrong. Sometimes our feeling is correct, especially when someone shows dishonest behavior. The important thing is to observe the person over time and to be open to new information.

In conclusion, first impression is a starting point, not a final decision. We should give people time before we make a judgment about them.

prompt: Write an essay about whether first impressions are accurate.
text:
We form first impressions in seconds, often before anyone says a word. A handshake, a tone of voice, or how someone dresses can shape our opinion long before we know anything real about them. Psychologists call this thin-slicing, and it isnt always a flaw. It helps us handle new situations fast, especially when time is short.

The trouble starts when we treat that first judgment as the final answer. Once we decide someone is unfriendly, we tend to notice what confirms it and ignore what doesnt. A student who seems aloof might just be shy or anxious or dealing with something at home. If we stop paying attention after the first meeting, we almost never find out.

Some first impressions are worth trusting though. Someone who keeps breaking promises or treats waiters with contempt tells you something important pretty quickly. Good instincts usually come from experience, so throwing out every first reaction would be just as dumb as believing all of them.

The smarter move is to treat first impressions like guesses you need to test. Notice what stood out, then check it with more interaction. Ask questions, listen, and watch how someone acts over time. That tells you way more than looks ever will.

First impressions matter because they open the door, but character decides whether anyone walks through. A good first impression might get you a conversation, but honesty and kindness over time are what make it a real relationship.

prompt: Write an essay about whether first impressions are accurate.

There's a thing my grandpa used to say about the way a man ties his shoes, which I think was supposed to mean something about character. I never understood it. He also thought everyone who wore sunglasses indoors was up to something, and he was wrong about most of them.

What I know is that first impressions are fast and lazy. They save you energy. But they also let you skip the part where you actually learn who someone is, which is slow and annoying and sometimes worth it.

prompt: Write an essay about whether it is better to work with a group or alone.
text:
Nowadays, many teachers ask students to work in groups for projects and presentations. Some students like this method, but others prefer to work alone. In my opinion, both options have advantages and disadvantages, but I think the group work is more important for our education because it prepares us for the real world.

The first advantage of working in groups is that we can share ideas and learn from each other. In my class of biology, we had to make a project about the ecosystems. My partner knew a lot about plants, and I knew more about animals. Together we created a presentation that was much better than what either of us could do alone. Also, group work teaches us to communicate and to negotiate. This is very useful in a job, where we need to work with different people every day.

However, the problem is that some students do not contribute. In my last group, one student did not come to the meetings and he did not send his part on time. Then we had to do his work at the last minute, and I was very stressed. It is not fair when one person is lazy and the others have to carry the responsibility.

On the other hand, working alone has its own benefits. Students can organize their time as they want and they do not depend on other people. When I write an essay, I need silence and concentration, and in a group it is very difficult. I can think more deeply and I can develop my own style.

In conclusion, I believe that the best solution is a balance between both methods. Teachers should give us some group projects to develop social skills, but also some individual tasks to develop our independence. In this way, we will be prepared for school and for our future work.

prompt: Write an essay about whether it is better to work with a group or alone.
text:
Nowadays, group work is very common in universities and high schools. Some students like to work with others, but some students think it is better to work alone. Personally, I think both ways have advantages, but the best choice depends on the task and the person.

Working in a group has many benefits. For example, last semester I took a marketing course and our group had to design a product for a company. Each member has different skills. One student was good at drawing, another was good at data, and I was responsible for the presentation. We finished the project in two weeks, which was faster than I expected. Moreover, I learned a lot from my classmates, because they had different ideas and experiences. I think this kind of cooperation is important for future work in a company.

However, group work also has problems. Sometimes some members do not do their part. In that course, one student disappeared for a week before the final presentation. We had to change the slides and the script very quickly. I was very tired and I was angry at him, but I could not say much because we were all in the same team.

When I work alone, I can control my schedule and my quality. I do not need to wait for other people or discuss every small detail. For example, when I wrote my thesis proposal, I work alone at the library every night. It was a quiet time for me to think and to write carefully. Working alone also give me confidence because I know the result is my own responsibility.

In my opinion, the ideal situation is to combine both methods. We can brainstorm together and then work separately on the details. This way, we can use the creativity of the group and the focus of an individual.

prompt: Write an essay about whether it is better to work with a group or alone.
text:
Few school assignments split students as much as group work. Some people like the chance to bounce ideas around, while others see it as a risk to their grade. Both reactions make sense. The right approach depends more on the task than on what you personally prefer.

Group work has real upsides. A team can mix different strengths, so one person handles research, another tightens the argument, and someone else builds the presentation. You also practice talking things through, compromising, and explaining your thinking to people who dont see it yet. Those skills rarely get taught directly, but employers care about them a lot.

Working alone gives you things a group cant. You can concentrate without interruptions and follow an idea wherever it goes, without arguing over every sentence. Solo work also makes responsibility simple. If the result is all yours, theres no question about who did what.

The main problem with group projects is uneven effort. When one person disappears before the deadline, everyone else ends up covering for them and still gets the same grade. Teachers can cut this down by giving clear roles, asking for individual reflections, and making groups show who did which part.

For most assignments, a mix is probably best. The team brainstorms and agrees on a direction, then each person develops their own piece on their own. You get the benefits of working together and still keep the focus and accountability of working solo.

prompt: Write an essay about whether cell phones should be allowed at school.
text:
Cell phones are part of our daily life, and now many students carry them to school. Some people think that schools should allow phones because they are useful, but others believe they are a distraction. In my opinion, cell phones should be permitted in school with strict rules, because they can help us learn but they must not interrupt the class.

First of all, cell phones are very useful educational tools. In my school in Peru, we did not have computers in every classroom, so when the teacher wanted us to research something, we used our phones. We could find dictionaries, maps, and videos about history or science. For students who do not have a laptop at home, the phone is sometimes the only way to access the internet. Also, in an emergency, parents can contact their children immediately, which gives families a sense of security.

However, phones can be a big problem during the lessons. Many students are looking at social media or playing games when they should be listening. I have seen students who cannot concentrate because they receive messages every minute. Moreover, cheating is easier with a phone, and this is unfair for the students who study honestly.

I think the school should create clear rules. For example, phones could be turned off during tests and during explanations, but they could be used during group activities that require research. Teachers also need to be trained to use technology in a good way.

In conclusion, cell phones are not good or bad by themselves. The result depends on how we use them. If the school teaches students to be responsible, the phone can be a helpful tool and not only a toy.

prompt: Write an essay about whether cell phones should be allowed at school.
text:
Nowadays, almost every student has a cell phone, so the question of whether phones should be allowed at school is very important. In my view, cell phones should not be used freely in class, but schools should not ban them completely either. The phone can be a good tool for learning if students use it at the right time.

In my middle school in China, cell phones were strictly forbidden. Students had to hand them to the teacher at the morning and get them back after school. At the beginning I felt very uncomfortable because I could not contact my parents during the day. Once my grandmother was sick and I could not know the news until I went home. However, I also think the rule helped us concentrate. In the class, nobody played games under the desk, and we could focus on the lessons. Teachers could also teach more effectively because they did not need to compete with the screens.

When I went to university in the United States, the situation was very different. Students use phones to check the schedule, to take notes, and to download reading materials. The professor sometimes asks us to answer questions on our phones during lectures. I think this is a good way to involve the students. But I also see some classmates who are shopping online during the class, which is a waste of money and time.

So, I believe schools should find a balance. Phones could be allowed during breaks and for educational purposes, but during important lessons and tests they should be turned off. Both teachers and students need to learn self-control, because the technology will not disappear. The question is how we use it, not whether we have it.

prompt: Write an essay about whether cell phones should be allowed at school.
text:
The debate over phones in school tends to get loud and not very useful. Supporters point to instant access to information. Critics describe constant distraction and temptation. Both have a point, which is why a total ban or no rules at all usually satisfies nobody.

Phones can actually help learning. Students can look up a definition, check a date, or record a lecture they missed. If you dont have a computer at home, your phone might be the only thing you can use for research and homework. Lots of schools also use phone apps for quizzes, reading, and class messages. Removing all of that ignores how students already live and learn.

The distractions are real though. A buzzing phone in your pocket can pull your attention away from a hard explanation, and social media is built to be hard to put down. Cheating is easier too, since answers and photos of test questions can get passed around in seconds. Teachers cant watch every screen in a crowded room.

A reasonable policy would separate allowed uses from disruptive ones. Phones could stay out during breaks and in specific activities, but get put away during tests and direct teaching. Clear expectations, consistent enforcement, and some training for teachers would make that easier to actually follow.

The goal shouldnt be shielding students from technology. It should be teaching them when and how to use it well. A phone isnt a villain or a teacher. What matters is the habits and limits around it.

prompt: Write an essay about the value of community service.
text:
Community service is an activity where people give their time to help others without receiving money. In my opinion, community service is very important for young people because it develops empathy and responsibility. It also helps the community to become stronger and more united.

When I was fifteen years old, I started to volunteer at a shelter for elderly people in my city. At the beginning, I was nervous because I did not know what to do. However, I helped the residents to read the newspaper and to play cards, and I listened to their stories. One of them was a woman who had worked as a teacher for forty years. She told me many things about the history of our town that I did not know. Since that time, I understand that the elderly people have a lot of wisdom and they need company.

Another benefit is that community service helps young people to develop skills. For example, my friend organized a campaign to clean the river near our school. She learned how to talk with the government and how to coordinate many volunteers. These experiences are very useful for future jobs, especially in universities where they ask for activities outside the classroom.

On the other hand, some people think that community service should not be obligatory. They say that students must do it because they like it, not because the school demands it. I understand this point of view, but I believe that obligation can be the first step. Many students who started by force later continued by their own decision.

To conclude, community service is a way to give something back to society. It is not only a requirement for school, but also an opportunity to change our perspective and to make our community a better place for everyone.

prompt: Write an essay about the value of community service.
text:
Community service is becoming more and more popular among young people. In my opinion, it is very meaningful activity because it allows people to help others and to learn new things. Although some students do it only for the certificate, I think community service can change a person's life in a good way.

Last summer I volunteered at a children's library in my neighborhood. The library was small and old, and it did not have enough books. My job was to read stories to children every Saturday and to help them with their homework. At first I was worried because I was not good at speaking to small kids. However, after a few weeks, they began to wait for me at the door. One boy, who was very shy, finally asked me to teach him how to draw a dragon. That moment made me feel very happy and useful.

Through this experience, I learned that community service is not only about giving things, but also about building relationships. I also learned patience and responsibility. When I started, I thought I would be the teacher, but actually I learned a lot from the children. They reminded me of the simple joys of life.

Some people argue that community service should be voluntary and not required by schools. I partly agree, because forced service can make students resentful. But I think schools should encourage it, because many students would never try it without some push. For example, my friend did not want to volunteer at first, but now she is the leader of a group that collects clothes for poor families.

In conclusion, community service is valuable for both the people who receive help and the people who give it. It builds empathy, and it shows young people that they can make a real difference in their community.

prompt: Write an essay about the value of community service.
text:
Community service is often treated as a box to tick on a college application. But the experience can show something more useful, which is how much ordinary people depend on each other. Volunteering puts students in conversation with neighbors whose lives look nothing like their own, and that contact tends to build empathy in ways textbooks don't.

Take a teenager who spends a semester tutoring kids at a local library. She might start out feeling obligated, but pretty soon she notices which kids struggle with reading, which parents work double shifts, and how much one patient adult can change a kid's confidence. Those things don't show up in class, and they can shape how students think about inequality for years.

It also builds real skills. Running a food drive means planning, communicating, and staying persistent when donations are unreliable. Students who coordinate volunteers learn to deal with adults, handle disappointment, and take responsibility for results they can't fully control.

Some critics have a fair point. When service is mandatory, some students resent it, and the relationship can feel like a transaction. The fix isn't to drop the requirement but to design it better, with meaningful roles and time to reflect instead of just counting hours.

Done well, community service does more than look good on a résumé. It shows young people their effort can improve a real place, and improvement usually starts by simply showing up.

prompt: Write an essay about why honesty matters.
text:
Honesty is one of the most valuable qualities that a person can have. In my opinion, being honest is important in friendship, in school, and in the work, because without honesty, the relationships are based on fear or lies. Although sometimes the truth can be painful, I believe that honesty always brings more benefits in the long term.

When I was living in Venezuela, I had a friend named Carlos who was very good at mathematics. We were in the same class, and during the final exam he asked me to show him my answers. I did not want to help him, but I also did not want to lose his friendship. I told him that I could not do it, because it was wrong. He was angry at me for a few days, but after that he came back and said that he was sorry. He explained that he was very afraid of failing his family. Since that day, we have been very close friends and he has never asked me to cheat again.

This experience taught me that honesty can be hard in the moment, but it creates trust. When people know that you tell the truth, they feel safe with you. On the other hand, when you lie, even a small lie, the other person will start to doubt everything that you say.

In the workplace, honesty is also important. My first job was in a store, and once I saw my manager take money from the register. I was very worried and I did not know what to do. Finally I decided to report it to the owner, and the manager lost his job. Some of my coworkers said I was a traitor, but the owner thanked me and gave me more responsibility.

In conclusion, honesty is not always easy, but it is the foundation of good relationships and a good society. I believe that we should practice it every day, even in small things.

prompt: Write an essay about why honesty matters.
text:
Honesty is a very important value in our society. Many people think that a little lie is harmless, but I think honesty is necessary in all parts of life, including friendship, school, and work. In my opinion, a honest person is more respected, even if the truth is sometimes uncomfortable.

Last year, I have a problem in my part-time job at a restaurant. One day, I broke a plate by accident while I was washing dishes. Nobody saw it, and I could easily hide the broken pieces in the trash. My manager was very busy, so I thought he would never know. However, I felt very bad about it. I could not sleep that night. The next morning, I went to the manager and told him what happened. I was afraid that he would be angry and maybe fire me. But he thanked me for telling the truth and he said the cost of the plate would be taken from my salary. Surprisingly, after that, he trusted me much more, and he gave me the responsibility of opening the store on weekends.

This experience taught me that honesty can protect our relationships. When we lie, we need to remember the lie and to protect it, which is very tiring. When we tell the truth, we feel relaxed and free. Also, other people feel that they can rely on us.

However, I think that honesty must be combined with kindness. For example, if my friend asks me about her new dress and I do not like it, I can say something positive about the color or the material. It is not necessary to be cruel. The goal is to be truthful without hurting people unnecessarily.

In conclusion, honesty is the basis of trust in both personal and social life. Although lying may seem easier in the short term, the truth always brings more peace and respect in the long run.

prompt: Write an essay about why honesty matters.
text:
Honesty gets praised all the time and bent just as often. People tell little lies to dodge awkward moments, protect feelings, or get out of trouble, and a lot of them figure those lies are harmless. But all those little things add up, and they slowly wear down the trust relationships depend on.

Honesty matters most when it costs you something. Owning up to a mistake in front of a teacher, giving back money you got by accident, or telling a friend something they dont want to hear all take guts. Small choices show character better than big speeches do, because they happen when nobody's watching and a convenient lie is right there.

You don't have to be cruel to be honest, though. You can tell the truth and still pick your words carefully, saying what's good before you get to what's wrong. The point is to avoid deceiving people, not to use honesty as an excuse to be harsh. Someone who says every thought out loud might be honest, but that doesn't make them wise or kind.

School is a big place to practice this. When students copy homework or hide cheating, they learn that dishonesty is an easy shortcut. When teachers handle honest mistakes fairly, they show that integrity is worth the discomfort.

Honesty is less about avoiding punishment than about being someone people can count on. Trust builds slowly through consistent truthfulness, and one discovered lie can wreck it fast.

I think honesty is less about the big moral stuff and more about giving people the chance to help. I robbed him of that for three months. Dumb.
